messages.subject: Dealing with label switching problem
parts:
I believe one way to deal with the label switching problem is to make sure your probability parameter on the states are ordered. I was thinking of doing something along the lines of:

parameters {
    simplex[K+1] pi;
    ...
  }
  transformed parameters {
    positive_ordered[K] pi_new;
    positive_ordered[K+1] tmp;

    tmp <- cumulative_sum(theta); //going to discard this variable
    pi_new <- head(tmp,K)/tmp[K+1];
    ...
  }

My question is do you need to worry about the Jacobian in this case? If so how do I incorporate the Jacbian calculation into the stan model (speaking in terms of syntax, not maths).

Thanks,
Sachin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Dealing with label switching problem
parts:
Whether you need a Jacobian depends on what you
do with pi_new. If you have pi_new on the left
of a ~ (literally or conceptually through increment_log_prob),
then you need a Jacobian.

I discuss that approach to the label-switching problem
in the problematic posteriors chapter of the manual. Ordering
changes the posterior; how dramatically depends on how close
your mixture components are to each other.

I didn't understand why you wanted to define pi_new the way
you did. Why not just define pi_new as a parameter directly?

Also, if you don't need to save tmp, you could define this as:

> transformed parameters {
> positive_ordered[K] pi_new;
> {
> positive_ordered[K+1] tmp;
> tmp <- cumulative_sum(theta); //going to discard this variable
}
> pi_new <- head(tmp,K)/tmp[K+1];

and then tmp is a local variable that won't be saved.

- Bob
